knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A supply-side leak is referred to a licence holder. The report records the referral in full and does not describe licensed work as completed.
Percentage savings are not promised without measurements. The business offers to measure and reports what the evidence supports.
Supply-side and plumbing repairs need a licence holder, so they are excluded from the business's agreement and offered as referrals.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied mock visit record with three zones and one supply-side fault, the learner writes a service report in the standard order with the referral separated from the in-scope work, within the assessor's set time.
The learner drafts the exclusions section of a supplied mock maintenance agreement, including supply-side, electrical and backflow work.
The learner responds in role-play to a request for a guaranteed water-saving percentage by offering a measured approach and no promise.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Service report for the mock visit, signed by the assessor.
Exclusions section for the mock agreement, reviewed by the assessor.
Assessor observation record of the role-play response.
stopWorkCriteria: Recording a supply-side repair as completed by the business during the assessment.
Making a percentage water-saving promise during the role-play.
